mediaStage.autoRedact: Blur sensitive data in new recordings
mediaStage.autoRedactHint: After a take, OCR finds e-mails, tenant domains, GUIDs, secrets and phone numbers on screen and blurs them. Each blur is a regular annotation you can keep or delete. Runs offline.
mediaStage.glossaryHint: Names the transcription is corrected to, one per line: Term: misheard 1, misheard 2. Applies to new transcriptions.
mediaStage.glossaryApplied: Glossary applied: {{count}} correction(s). Undo with Ctrl+Z.
mediaStage.glossaryNothingToFix: Nothing to fix: the transcripts already follow the glossary.
mediaStage.modelHint: The accurate model is downloaded on the first transcription and runs on a dedicated GPU. Automatic uses it when the GPU has room for it, and the fast one otherwise.
mediaStage.standingTermsHint: Whisper is told to expect these terms in every transcription, before the project's names and terms. Separate them with commas; the first ones matter most.
mediaStage.redactTermsHint: Names, words and numbers to blur too, one per line. Case and accents do not matter, and a match inside a longer word blurs that word.
mediaStage.redactRescanHint: Read this project's recordings again and replace the automatic blurs. Blurs you drew stay.
mediaStage.redactRescanFailed: The recordings could not be read again.
mediaStage.redactRescanNothing: Nothing changed: the automatic blurs are already up to date.
mediaStage.redactRescanDone: Automatic blurs updated: {{added}} added, {{removed}} replaced. Undo with Ctrl+Z.
mediaStage.transcribeGuest: Transcribe the computer sound too (call guest)
mediaStage.transcribeGuestHint: For a take with separate voice and computer tracks: transcribes both and marks who said each word. Off: only your microphone is transcribed.

mcpServer.title: MCP server
mcpServer.description: Let MCP clients you run yourself, such as Claude Code or Codex, use the AI editing tools on any of your projects, not only the one open in the editor. They sign in with their own accounts; OpenScreen never sees them.
mcpServer.allowEdits: Allow MCP clients to edit your projects
mcpServer.editsHint: Off by default: clients can read your projects, and every edit they try is refused. When on, each edit is saved as it lands; an edit to the project open in the editor can be undone there.
mcpServer.tokenHint: Clients must send this token. Regenerating it disconnects every client set up with the old one.
mcpServer.codexHint: Codex reads the token from the {{env}} environment variable. Set it in the shell you start Codex from.
